In [[mathematics]], the '''Alperin–Brauer–Gorenstein theorem''' characterizes the [[finite simple group]]s with [[quasidihedral]] or wreathed<ref>A [[p-group|2-group]] is '''wreathed''' if it is a [[nonabelian group|nonabelian]] [[semidirect product]] of a [[maximal subgroup]] that is a [[direct product of groups|direct product]] of two [[cyclic group]]s of the same [[order (group theory)|order]], that is, if it is the [[wreath product]] of a cyclic 2-group with the [[symmetric group]] on 2 points.</ref> [[Sylow subgroup|Sylow 2-subgroups]]. These are [[group isomorphism|isomorphic]] either to three-dimensional [[projective special linear group]]s or [[projective special unitary group]]s over a [[finite field]] of odd order, depending on a certain congruence, or to the [[Mathieu group]] <math>M_{11}</math>.  {{harvtxt|Alperin|Brauer|Gorenstein|1970}} proved this in the course of 261 pages.  The subdivision by 2-fusion is sketched there, given as an exercise in {{harvtxt|Gorenstein|1968|loc=Ch. 7}}, and presented in some detail in {{harvtxt|Kwon|Lee|Cho|Park|1980}}.
